category_title: High-academic kindergartner with ASD who uses classroom scripts for social interaction
minimal_context: Jasmine is sitting at a round table with a peer and a paraprofessional to complete a math worksheet where she needs to color objects in groups of four.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time to complete your math worksheet. Please color the objects on the page in groups of four.

STUDENT: Let’s do some colors! What color is the apple? What color is the boy? What color is the car?

TUTOR: Jasmine, please look at your own paper. You need to do your math.

STUDENT: (Excitedly shakes her braids and rubs her fingers together quickly in front of the ABC book) O the O says/ o/, octopus. the T says…

TUTOR: (Points to the math worksheet) You cannot read the ABC book right now. We have music next, so you need to do your math.

STUDENT: (Grabs the ABC book again) No! Aaahh!

options.A: Ask higher-order questions while engaging in the math worksheet, provide a more challenging alternative activity, or turn the activity into an opportunity for social interaction.
options.B: Use responsive digital media that allows selecting colors from an on-screen palette and tapping a section of the math worksheet to color it in automatically.
options.C: Calmly direct Jasmine to avoid grabbing the ABC book and to use her crayon. After one prompt, withhold attention for grabbing the book.
options.D: Ask Jasmine the name of the letter in the ABC book, prompting her by saying: "This one, you know it, it's in your name."
